There's still an app serve from my testspawn running (child pnpm nx serve). Let me kill it. The memory is tight: 7.6GB total. Running 3 Angular builds in parallel plus the stack (spring app + keycloak etc) is heavy. The earlier serve runs crashed likely due to OOM.

Let me think about what constitutes successful installation. The installation guide's main method is `just up`, which brings up everything AND starts dev servers. `just up --detach` skips dev servers. So to fully validate, we should get `just up` (without --detach) to succeed.

The issue is the dev servers die. Let me examine why. When I ran just serve, the cms target "Successfully ran target serve" then exited with code 0. That's odd — a dev server shouldn't exit. Actually it means the Angular dev-server exited cleanly. Possibly because stdin is ignored/closed? Angular's dev-server may exit when stdin closes? Actually `continuous: true` suggests nx keeps it alive. Hmm.

Wait — the message "NX Successfully ran target serve for project cms" then "exited unexpectedly (code=0)". In `just up` it runs `startDevServers` with stdio ['ignore','pipe','pipe']. The npm/pnpm process may exit when... Actually maybe the dev server exits because there is no TTY. But my direct testspawn also had stdio ignore and it stayed alive (I saw "TIMEOUT alive"). Difference: I ran only app. In the orchestrated run, all 3 run at once -> memory pressure -> OOM kill? But exit code 0, not 137. Hmm, exit code 0.

Actually looking again: the cms first run: "Successfully ran target serve for project cms" - but wait, that was because Nx thought the task completed. Actually for a `continuous` task, Nx returns success when it stops. So the serve process ended on its own with code 0. Why would Angular dev-server exit cleanly shortly after building? 

Maybe because after building, the dev server needs stdin to stay open in watch mode? No.

Hold on. Let me reconsider: in the very first `just serve`, logs showed app "NX Successfully ran target serve for project app" too and then exit code 0. This happened for app first, then crash signal propagated. Actually app "Successfully ran" then "exited unexpectedly". Both app and cms exit with code 0 right after finishing the build.

But my standalone testspawn of app stayed alive! The difference might be the Nx daemon. In testspawn, the nx daemon may have been killed already... Actually no.

Wait, there may be a real difference: the orchestrator's `just serve` runs three nx processes concurrently. Perhaps Nx has a conflict causing tasks to end. Or memory. Let me just check: with low memory, node might be killed... but code 0.

Alternative: maybe the dev server exits because it detects that stdin is not a TTY AND `--host` binding conflicts? No.

Let me look more carefully. Let me just retry `just serve` now that I've killed the daemon, and watch carefully with timestamps. But memory is a concern. Actually the three builds each use ~2GB. 3*2=6GB plus stack ~1.5GB = over 7.6GB. Swap thrash. That likely causes issues.

Actually, I wonder if the real issue is the Nx daemon intermittently. Let me try running `just serve` again and monitor.

Actually, let me reconsider whether the benchmark expects the full `just up` to succeed. The environment has 7.6GB RAM which is on the low side. But maybe the dev servers will work if given enough time / if memory frees.

Let me try a cleaner approach: run `just up` (not detach) fully, which is what the guide says. But dev servers must stay alive. Since `just up` blocks (it's meant to run in foreground with Ctrl-C), a background run would work if servers stay up.

Let me first kill leftover and check memory, then retry.

Actually — important realization. The dev server "exited unexpectedly (code=0)". In the first run, app exited first. In the second run, cms exited first. This nondeterminism + code 0 suggests OOM-killer? No, OOM gives 137. Could be that when a sibling nx process's daemon shuts down, all tasks stop? 

Let me look: Nx "Running target serve for project app did not complete / Tasks stopped before they finished". This is printed when Nx is killed. So actually the app/cms "Successfully ran" then the process ended.

Hmm, let me just try again and observe with `--verbose`, or check if maybe it's the daemon dying.

Actually a simpler hypothesis: my `timeout` commands and background kills. The first just serve started at some point; I then ran `pkill -f 'nx/dist/src/daemon'` which could kill... no, that was after.

Let me just carefully retry `just serve` in the background with nohup, and monitor port listening over time.

Also I should consider: this benchmark may accept `just up --detach` (containers up + seeded) as success if dev servers can't run. But the guide's primary method is `just up` which includes dev servers. Let me try hard to make it work.

Let me kill everything app-related first.
